Zinit is a Zsh loader and has no single universal selected-plugin configuration
The due-update case measures a declined prompt; it does not execute an update or access a network

observation.order: alternate case order by pair and run
observation.terminal: 32 rows, 120 columns, 8 MiB output limit, 10 second phase timeout
observation.accepted_input: after editor input mode, type colon and require execution acknowledgment and next prompt; record observer echo quiet interval
observation.priming: one fully effect-checked untimed launch before timings; source preparation and template installation remain outside launch timing
observation.home: separate private home and copied framework tree per case; synthetic history reset outside timed fields; ble.sh runs from a private build copy and creates its own cache there
observation.system_completion_inputs: record presence and SHA256 for system Bash-completion entry points and Git completion search matches, plus tool identities; system packages remain outside the pinned upstream archives
observation.updates: template updater remains enabled, not-due and due-decline are distinct cases; automatic decline prevents network calls
observation.integrity: pinned source archive and build-output inventories checked before and after each run; driver, contract, executable and case identities checked at pair boundaries; dynamic private state recorded at launch boundaries
observation.resources: readiness observation only; non-atomic approximate RSS, shared pages counted per process, vanished children explicit; no peak or overall ranking
observation.failure: any setup, identity, prompt or effect failure rejects the run and retains all completed observations and partial evidence
